2. illegal pairs set to minus infinity

g.data-tip: One scaled dot product for every ordered pair of positions. Nothing here knows about time: position 1 has a perfectly good score against position 4.
Every entry whose key index exceeds its query index is overwritten with minus infinity. This happens to the input of the softmax, not to its output.
Exponentiating minus infinity gives exactly zero, so the blocked cells contribute nothing to the weighted sum and no gradient flows back through them.

a.data-tip: Section 3.2.3 places the mask inside scaled dot-product attention, on the input of the softmax. That placement is what makes the zeros exact rather than merely small.
a.text: Exactly what is set to minus infinity, and exactly where
Section 3.2.3: the mask is applied inside scaled dot-product attention, to all values in the input of the
softmax which correspond to illegal connections. Illegal means every pair where j is greater than i.
Because the mask hits the scores and not the outputs, the softmax turns those cells into exact zeros:
no value from a future token is summed in, and no gradient flows backwards in time through them.
Together with the output embedding being offset by one position, this is what keeps the decoder autoregressive.
